two-way: the reversible 6-block engine (fly-horizontal-6b-10gt-01ce95: two sticky pistons, the one that fires first sets the direction) shuttling between two 4-block return stations: an obsidian wall stops it; an observer watching the cell only the trailing observer enters at the stop fires 2 gt later into a block whose cross dust points into the back of the leading part's sticky piston, which pushes the trailing part back (2 gt pulse: spit) and the engine runs the other way.

Payload family: the 6-block engine fly-horizontal-6b-10gt-e2cf52 carrying n blocks, 10 gt/block for every n: a column up from the front slime (slime, each drags the next; the top block gold), 9 at most (a piston moves at most 12 blocks: the 3-block part + 9), then a column down from the rear slime; n = 18 is the most the engine moves (a 10th block on the rear: the pull fails).

Train family: the 6-block engine fly-horizontal-6b-10gt-e2cf52 pulling n trailers, 10 gt/block for every n. A sticky piston on the rear slime (facing back, fired with the pusher by the rear observer) reach-pulls trailer 1 each cycle; every trailer but the last carries a sticky piston facing back and a rider observer (it fires into the trailer's slime 2 gt after the trailer lands) that pulls the next trailer, which starts against that piston's face. Each trailer is a piston move of its own (12 blocks at most), so the machine has no size limit: 5 + 3n blocks (a two-part machine moves at most 24).
